svg.text: The character of the building — read through its outliers
In statistics, an outlier is what falls outside the expected range — a deviation.
In architecture, the outliers are the signature spaces — the courtyard, the long corridor,
the buried workshop. Statistical anomalies reveal architectural identity.
A single 2766 m² courtyard. A 636 m² studio.
Most rooms are 30–90 m². The exceptions are
How many other spaces does each space touch?
Almost every room has exactly 1 neighbour.
A few corridors connect to 40+. They are the
How far is each space from everywhere else?
Most rooms sit 3.7 to 4.3 steps deep. The
workshops live in the building's pockets.
The most integrated rooms are not where you'd
expect. Two corridors and a quiet faculty
A single space — the courtyard — appears as an outlier across three of four metrics. It is both the biggest, the most connected, and the most central.
The 2nd-floor corridors (#301, #320) are extreme topology outliers: each links 40+ rooms. Without them the barracks plan would fall apart.
The basement holds the depth outliers — workshops and archives. Production-heavy programs inherit the original service-zone logic.
Outliers identified via the IQR method (1.5×IQR rule). All values computed from the 181-room dataset.
